Searched for
harmonic-bar|scale|transform|hover
Now let me look at the current CSS for the harmonic bars to understand the transformation behavior:

Read
src/index.css
Perfect! Now I understand the issue. Let me analyze the braid bubble scaling architecture:

🎯 BRAID HALF-BUBBLE SCALING ANALYSIS
🔍 Current Architecture Understanding
Looking at the YinYangCircle component, I can see the structure:

Dual Bubble System: Each "bubble" is actually a yin-yang circle with two interactive half-bubbles
Current Transform Origin: The CSS shows transform-origin: bottom for general harmonic bars, but SVG elements have transform: none !important
Center Point: Each circle has a center at (cx, cy) with radius r
Half-Bubble Paths:
Top half (Yin): blackPath - covers from cy-r to cy
Bottom half (Yang): whitePath - covers from cy to cy+r
⚠️ The Transform Origin Problem
You're absolutely right about the anchor point issue! Currently:

Problem: If we scale a half-bubble, it would scale from its own geometric center
Top Half: Would scale from around cy - r/2 (middle of top half)
Bottom Half: Would scale from around cy + r/2 (middle of bottom half)
Result: Half-bubbles would scale away from each other instead of toward the shared center
🎯 Solution Architecture

Flowchart
📋 Implementation Strategy
1. SVG Group Structure

<g transform-origin={`${cx} ${cy}`}>
  {/* Top half-bubble with center-based scaling */}
  <path 
    d={blackPath} 
    style={{
      transformOrigin: `${cx}px ${cy}px`,
      transform: topSelected ? 'scale(1.1)' : 'scale(1)'
    }}
  />
  
  {/* Bottom half-bubble with center-based scaling */}
  <path 
    d={whitePath} 
    style={{
      transformOrigin: `${cx}px ${cy}px`, 
      transform: bottomSelected ? 'scale(1.1)' : 'scale(1)'
    }}
  />
</g>
2. CSS Transform Origin Override

/* Override the SVG transform restrictions for scaling */
svg .harmonic-bar.scaling {
  transform: initial !important;
  transform-origin: var(--bubble-center-x) var(--bubble-center-y);
  transition: transform 0.2s ease-out;
}

svg .harmonic-bar.scaling.selected {
  transform: scale(1.1) !important;
}
3. Z-Index Layering Solution

/* Layering system for overlapping half-bubbles */
svg .harmonic-bar {
  z-index: 1;
}

svg .harmonic-bar.selected {
  z-index: 10; /* Selected half-bubble appears on top */
}

svg .harmonic-bar.neighbor-selected {
  z-index: 5; /* Adjacent half-bubble gets intermediate layer */
}
🚨 Potential Layering Issues & Solutions
Issue 1: SVG Z-Index Limitations
Problem: SVG doesn't honor CSS z-index - rendering order is DOM order
Solution: Dynamically reorder DOM elements or use SVG <use> with <defs>
Issue 2: Overlap Collision
Problem: Scaled half-bubbles will overlap their partners
Solution: Coordinated scaling - when one scales up, its partner scales down slightly
Issue 3: Visual Hierarchy
Problem: Which half-bubble appears "on top" when both are selected?
Solution: Last-interacted gets priority, or use alpha blending
🔧 Recommended Implementation Plan
Phase 1: Center-Anchored Scaling

const getHalfBubbleTransform = (isSelected: boolean, isPartner: boolean) => {
  if (isSelected) {
    return `scale(1.12)`;
  }
  if (isPartner) {
    return `scale(0.95)`; // Partner scales down slightly
  }
  return `scale(1)`;
};

// Apply to each path with center origin
style={{
  transformOrigin: `${cx}px ${cy}px`,
  transform: getHalfBubbleTransform(topSelected, bottomSelected)
}}
Phase 2: Dynamic DOM Reordering

// Reorder selected elements to render last (on top)
const orderedElements = useMemo(() => {
  const elements = [topElement, bottomElement];
  return elements.sort((a, b) => {
    if (a.selected && !b.selected) return 1;
    if (!a.selected && b.selected) return -1;
    return 0;
  });
}, [topSelected, bottomSelected]);
Phase 3: Coordinated Animation

.harmonic-bar.scaling {
  transition: transform 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
}
💡 Creative Solutions for Layering
Alpha Blending: Use opacity changes instead of strict layering
Staggered Scaling: Animate scales with slight timing offsets
Outline Enhancement: Increase stroke-width on selected elements
Glow Differentiation: Use different glow colors for layering cues
This approach ensures that half-bubbles scale from the center of the dual system while managing overlaps elegantly. The key is coordinating the scaling behavior so the visual hierarchy remains clear and intuitive.
